title: Places to Visit Near Nagpur Under 100 km
summary: From Pench tiger safaris to Gandhi's ashram at Sevagram and carved temples at Markanda, here are the best places near Nagpur within 100 km.
body_markdown:
Pench and Ramtek are the names most Nagpur residents reach for first. But the places to visit near Nagpur under 100 km go considerably deeper than those two: Gupta-period ruins at Mansar, a 9th century carved temple complex at Markanda, and Gandhi’s working ashram at Sevagram in Wardha, all sitting within a morning’s drive of the city.


This guide covers eight verified destinations, organized by what they offer rather than a simple ranking. Whether you are arriving in Nagpur from another city or already based here, book your[Nagpur bus](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/nagpur-bus-booking-online) through zingbus and use this guide to plan the following day’s drive.


# **Places to Visit Near Nagpur Under 100 km**


Four types of experience sit within this radius: wildlife, heritage, spiritual, and open nature. The places to visit near Nagpur under 100 km are more varied than the city’s own residents tend to give them credit for, and most of them draw a fraction of the footfall they deserve on any given weekend.


## **Wildlife Near Nagpur: Pench National Park**


Pench National Park sits 78 km from Nagpur on NH44 toward Seoni and is the closest major tiger reserve to any large city in Maharashtra. The park spans more than 750 sq km of mixed teak forest across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, with the Pench River cutting through the center and creating the waterholes and river corridors where wildlife concentrates.


Safaris run at dawn and dusk in open jeeps with a guide. The dawn slot is where most sightings happen. Tiger activity is highest in the first two hours after gate opening, particularly near the river corridor. The park supports Bengal tigers, leopards, Indian wild dogs, sloth bears, gaur, and over 285 bird species, making it one of the better birding destinations in Central India alongside its wildlife reputation.


Bookings open 90 days in advance through the Maharashtra Forest Department portal. Weekend slots between October and February fill within days of going live. Leave Nagpur before 4:30 AM to reach the gate for the dawn session. October through March is the productive wildlife season. The Maharashtra zone closes from approximately July 1 to October 1 for monsoon.


## **Heritage Sites Near Nagpur Within 100 km**


Three sites within this radius carry heritage significance well beyond their visitor numbers.


### **Ramtek**


Ramtek is 40 km from Nagpur and centers on the Ram Temple complex built on Ramgiri Hill. The climb to the top takes about 20 minutes on stone steps and gives a clear view across the Vidarbha plains. The Kalidasa Smarak at the base of the hill is what most people skip: tradition holds that the Sanskrit poet Kalidasa composed the Meghaduta here, watching monsoon clouds drift northward across this valley. The hillside and the lake below it match the poem’s description closely enough to make the stop genuinely interesting.


### **Mansar**


Mansar sits 65 km from Nagpur and is an active Archaeological Survey of India site with Gupta-period ruins dated to the 5th century CE. Excavations have produced terracotta figurines, copper coins, and structural remains pointing to a settlement that served Buddhist and Hindu communities simultaneously. The site rewards visitors who arrive with some background reading. Without it, the remains read as open ground with old walls. With it, you are standing inside a settlement that was active 1,500 years ago.


### **Markanda**


Markanda at 95 km sits right at the edge of this radius and earns the drive. The 8th to 9th century rock-cut temple complex near the Wainganga River is sometimes called the Khajuraho of Vidarbha, a comparison the carvings justify. Panels of deities, celestial figures, and decorative motifs in basalt are detailed and well-preserved. There is no tourist infrastructure here. Carry food and water because nothing is available at the site.


## **Spiritual Stops Near Nagpur**


### **Koradi Temple**


Koradi is 15 km from Nagpur, making it the closest significant religious site on this list. The Mahalakshmi complex sits beside a lake and is quiet on regular weekday mornings. Navratri brings large crowds. For residents who want a few hours outside the city without planning a full trip, Koradi works as a standalone morning visit.


### **Adasa Ganesh Temple**


Adasa Ganesh Temple, 50 km from Nagpur, belongs to the Ashta-Vinayak circuit of the Vidarbha region. The self-manifested Ganesha idol stands 12 feet tall and is among the larger examples in Maharashtra. The temple draws pilgrims mainly during festival periods rather than year-round, so a non-festival visit is uncrowded and straightforward.


## **Gandhi’s Ashram at Sevagram, Wardha**


Gandhi chose Sevagram in 1936 as his base, specifically over larger cities like Nagpur, and lived here through independence. The ashram is 78 km from Nagpur and is preserved exactly as he left it. Bapu Kuti, Adi Niwas, and Bahen Niwas are the original mud and brick structures where Gandhi slept, worked, and met political figures. The spinning wheel sits on the table. His daily schedule is handwritten on the wall. There are no reconstructions, no audio guides, no additions of any kind.


The scale is what the visit turns on. Gandhi’s personal room is smaller than most contemporary studio flats. That smallness tells the story more directly than any exhibition could. Allow three hours. Include the adjacent Maganwadi, where Gandhi ran rural industry programs, before leaving. Entry is free. Open 6:30 AM to 6 PM daily.


## **Lakes and Nature Near Nagpur**


Khindsi Lake, 60 km from Nagpur, is a reservoir with boating facilities, a garden area, and basic food stalls along the lakefront. It works as a family half-day outing rather than a standalone travel destination. November through February is a comfortable window. Arriving before 10 AM on weekends gives you the lake before the afternoon crowds arrive.


## **Seasonal Guide for Nagpur Day Trips**


October through March covers all eight destinations without any seasonal obstacles. Wildlife conditions at Pench are best as vegetation thins and animals concentrate near water. Heritage sites like Sevagram, Ramtek, and Markanda are most comfortable in cool, dry weather. Vidarbha’s summer from April through June regularly pushes above 42 degrees Celsius, making outdoor sites difficult. Pench’s Maharashtra zone closes between July and September. Temples and indoor sites remain accessible year-round.

## **Before You Drive Out of Nagpur**


Pench safari slots for October through February weekends fill within days of the 90-day booking window opening. Log your travel date and set a reminder for the Maharashtra Forest Department portal.


Carry sufficient cash before leaving Nagpur. ATMs near Ramtek, Mansar, Markanda, and Khindsi are unreliable. Entry fees at Pench, Mansar, and Markanda are modest but cash-only at the gate.


Sevagram is significantly quieter on weekdays. School groups and tour parties arrive on weekends and change the character of the ashram. A Tuesday or Wednesday morning visit gives you the place closer to what it actually is.


For Markanda, there is no shade or shelter near the temple complex. Plan to arrive before 9 AM and leave before noon if visiting between March and October.


## **The Places to Visit Near Nagpur Under 100 km That Reward the Drive**


Nagpur’s central location is a geography class fact that most residents do not cash in on. Within 100 km, the surrounding terrain holds a national park that closes the gap with India’s best tiger reserves, two protected archaeological sites from different historical periods, a Gandhian heritage complex of genuine global significance, and temple carvings that match some of the country’s most celebrated medieval stonework.


The places to visit near Nagpur under 100 km are not experiences you extract in transit. Pench gives back more when you have a booked safari and a dawn departure. Sevagram gives back more when you allow three hours instead of one. Markanda gives back more when you understand what the carvings represent before you stand in front of them. Each of these is a Saturday that becomes a better one the more preparation goes into it.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the most popular place to visit near Nagpur within 100 km?**


Pench National Park at 78 km is the most visited destination near Nagpur, known for consistent Bengal tiger sightings and as the landscape behind Rudyard Kipling’s The Jungle Book.


### **Is Pench National Park suitable for a day trip from Nagpur?**


Pench works well as a day trip if you leave Nagpur before 4:30 AM to reach the gate in time for the dawn safari slot.


### **What is the best season to visit places near Nagpur under 100 km?**


October through March is the best season, covering comfortable weather for outdoor heritage sites and optimal safari conditions at Pench.


### **Is Sevagram Ashram in Wardha worth visiting from Nagpur?**


Sevagram Ashram at 78 km from Nagpur is Gandhi’s preserved working complex, unchanged since independence, and one of the most authentic Gandhian heritage sites in India.


### **What are the main heritage sites within 100 km of Nagpur?**


The three main heritage sites are Ramtek at 40 km, Mansar at 65 km, and Markanda at 95 km, all maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India with distinct historical periods.


### **What is Markanda near Nagpur?**


Markanda is an 8th to 9th century rock-cut temple complex near the Wainganga River, about 95 km from Nagpur, with carved stone panels that rival Khajuraho in quality.


### **How far is Koradi Temple from Nagpur?**


Koradi Temple is approximately 15 km from Nagpur’s city center and is the closest significant religious site in this guide.


### **Is Khindsi Lake good for a family outing from Nagpur?**


Khindsi Lake at 60 km has boating facilities, open lakeside space, and basic food, making it a practical family half-day outing between November and February.


### **What is special about Adasa Ganesh Temple near Nagpur?**


Adasa Ganesh Temple, about 50 km from Nagpur, is part of the Vidarbha Ashta-Vinayak circuit and holds a self-manifested Ganesha idol standing 12 feet tall, one of the larger examples in Maharashtra.


### **What is Mansar near Nagpur?**


Mansar is a Gupta-period archaeological site 65 km from Nagpur, dated to the 5th century CE, with excavated remains pointing to an active religious and civic settlement that predates most heritage sites in Central India.


### **Does zingbus connect Nagpur to these day trip destinations?**

### **Can you visit more than one destination near Nagpur in a single day?**


Yes, combining two nearby sites works well: Koradi and Ramtek make a practical morning pair, while Mansar and Khindsi Lake are at similar distances and fit a full day at a relaxed pace.
